findings.text: the exemption is derived from the section's newest recorded activity, so a comment added after the fixed instant to a section that was already done removes its exemption and the close is refused, where docs/plans/a-landing-is-recorded-once.html:49 says such a section stays exempt however its plan is later edited. Reproduced at 842b7a8b: _landed_before_the_rule with a single 2026-11-01 comment on s1 returns True, and adding a 2026-11-15T12:00:00Z comment on the same section returns False. The remedy is a per-section tick time, keying on the earliest recorded activity rather than the newest, or a plan edit recording the narrower ruling; the live pass clears 174 of 174 open plans, so the effect is latent, and the refusal names the section and is recoverable.

`_readable_instant` duplicates the ISO-stamp-to-aware-UTC parser the repository already owns at reckon/_timestamps.py:36 (parse_utc), whose module docstring asks every timestamp reader to migrate to it and which twenty modules already import; it duplicates rather than extends or wraps the owner, since parse_utc gives the same None-on-malformed and naive-means-UTC behaviour and also accepts numeric epochs.
